title: Trent Williams' 12 Pro Bowls: An OU Tackle Among the NFL's Best
question: How many Pro Bowls has former Oklahoma tackle Trent Williams made?
answer: Twelve. Trent Williams (OU 2006-09), the No. 4 pick in the 2010 NFL Draft, earned his 12th Pro Bowl selection for the 2025 season, making him one of only four offensive linemen in NFL history with 12 or more.
summary: Former Sooner Trent Williams has 12 Pro Bowl nods, joining Bruce Matthews, Randall McDaniel and Will Shields among the NFL's most honored offensive linemen.
body: Trent Williams (OU 2006-09) came to Norman from Longview, Texas, and started at right tackle as a true freshman for Bob Stoops. By the end of his career he was a two-time first-team All-Big 12 pick and a consensus All-American in 2009.

Washington drafted him fourth overall in 2010, part of Oklahoma's historic night when three Sooners went in the first four picks. He grew into one of the league's premier left tackles, earning seven straight Pro Bowl selections during his time in Washington.

In April 2020 he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers, whose coach, Kyle Shanahan, had been part of the Washington staff that drafted him, and his second act may have been even better. He was a first-team All-Pro three years running, from 2021 through 2023, and he anchored the line for the 49ers team that reached Super Bowl LVIII, a 25-22 overtime loss to Kansas City.

In December 2025 the 49ers announced his 12th career Pro Bowl selection, his fifth in San Francisco. According to the team, that puts him in rare company: only Bruce Matthews, with 14, has more Pro Bowls among offensive linemen, while Randall McDaniel and Will Shields also reached 12.
For Sooner fans keeping score, that makes Williams arguably the most honored offensive lineman OU has ever sent to the NFL.
